title: Structure Mapping Theory
description: Gentner's structure mapping: analogy aligns relational structure, not surface features — the solar system maps to the atom via 'revolves around' and 'attracts', not via 'is hot'. Systematicity prefers deeply connected relational matches.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(1001)
# Structure-mapping similarity between two relational graphs (solar system vs atom).
# Relations as (rel, arg1, arg2); similarity = shared relational structure.
solar=[("revolves","earth","sun"),("attracts","sun","earth"),("revolves","mars","sun"),("hotter","sun","earth")]
atom=[("revolves","electron","nucleus"),("attracts","nucleus","electron"),("revolves","proton","nucleus"),("hotter","nucleus","electron")]
def relset(g): return set(r for r,_,_ in g)
rs, ra = relset(solar), relset(atom)
shared = rs & ra
# systematicity bonus: connected shared relations
score = len(shared)/max(len(rs|ra),1)
print(f"solar_relations={sorted(rs)}")
print(f"shared={sorted(shared)} structural_similarity={score:.2f}")
print("mapping: sun->nucleus, earth->electron (relational, not surface)")
print("DEMO_OK")
demo.output:
solar_relations=['attracts', 'hotter', 'revolves']
shared=['attracts', 'hotter', 'revolves'] structural_similarity=1.00
mapping: sun->nucleus, earth->electron (relational, not surface)
DEMO_OK
demo.note: Runnable demo program verified by execution during the database build.

architecture: Source and target are encoded as relational graphs; the matcher finds the maximal structurally consistent mapping. Surface-feature matches are discounted; relational matches score.
